subject: POC Kickoff Recap - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 20:30:00 -0800
Subject: POC Kickoff Recap - Acme Corp

Thanks again for a productive kickoff earlier today - wanted to capture the key items, owners, and next steps so we're all aligned. TL;DR: Redwood will run a 6-week pilot scoped to Acme's customer support triage workflow; success metrics, access items, and prompt/eval plan are below.

Scope (what we agreed):
- Inference integration for triage/enrichment pipeline on support cases (English).
- Intake: up to 500 requests/hour initially; target steady-state 1k req/hr by end of pilot.
- Focus on two features: 1) automated routing suggestions, 2) summary + suggested replies.

Pain points + goals (Acme):
- Agents spend ~4-6 min per ticket on categorization and initial reply.
- High variance in response quality; want consistent SLAs and faster TTR.
- Goal: reduce average handle time by 30% and improve first-reply accuracy to 85% on evaluated prompt set.

Success metrics (how we'll measure POC):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for generation-only endpoints (when batched).
- Quality: target 85% pass rate on Acme eval set (see prompt_set_v1.jsonl).
- Cost: baseline unit cost target <$0.50 per 1k tokens (we'll track during pilot).
- Uptime/availability: 99.5% during business hours.

Owners & contacts:
- Customer success / program lead: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai) - overall POC coordination.
- Solutions Eng (onboarding & evals): Neha Kapoor (neha.kapoor@redwood.ai).
- Runtime / SRE escalation: Rishi Malhotra (rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai).
- Acme POC leads: Jordan Reyes (Jordan.Reyes@acme.com), Priya Shah (Priya.Shah@acme.com).

Timeline / milestones (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): access + sample data transfer, confirm prompt set, finalize SOW.
- Week 1: initial model selection + baseline evals on sample data.
- Week 2-3: staging integration, iterative prompt tuning, and evals.
- Week 4: pilot runs on limited traffic (shadow/dual-write).
- Week 5-6: production-like run, final metrics + SOW sign-off.

Access / setup items required from Acme: (please share by EOD Mon)
1) IAM role ARN or a secure S3 bucket with sample data (manifest attached: acme-sample-data-manifest.csv).
2) Test Okta/SSO account or allowlist of 3 test emails for evaluation.
3) Sample of ~1k anonymized tickets (CSV/JSONL) for the baseline eval.
4) Preferred models (or allow Redwood to propose); see notes in prompt_set_v1.jsonl.

Prompt set & evals
- Attached: prompt_set_v1.jsonl - this is our initial eval set and rubric. Neha will run a baseline and share the first pass results.

Attachments: redwood-poc-sow.pdf (draft SOW), prompt_set_v1.jsonl, acme-sample-data-manifest.csv

Immediate next steps
- Jordan/Priya: confirm procurement timeline and who will own the SOW/doc signature (cc procurement).
- Acme: share IAM role or S3 link + sample data by Mon.
- Neha: will provision a staging endpoint and kick off baseline eval once data arrives.
- Marissa/Aditya: schedule weekly check-ins (I'll send a recurring invite).

If this captures everything, I'll upload the doc to Drive and send a DocuSign link for the SOW. Thanks - excited to get started.


Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - this is perfect and aligns with our internal notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement: Procurement will need the final SOW + pricing attachment to route for approval; target approval is by Jan 28 (we'll do our best). I cc'd procurement@acme.com.
- Data: We can provision an S3 bucket and either create a cross-account role or share via a presigned URL. I'll follow up with the DevOps owner to get an ARN by Monday.
- Eval set: The 1k anonymized tickets are available, but we need to redact PII - we'll deliver those as JSONL.

Two questions: 
1) Can Redwood support a shadow deployment model so we can compare outputs without impacting current flows?
2) For the latency target, is the p95 200ms measured from Redwood API receive->first token or end-to-end (including network)?

Thanks - we're excited to move quickly.

Jordan
Jordan Reyes
Head of Automation | Acme Corp
jordan.reyes@acme.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC Kickoff Recap - Acme Corp

Hi Jordan / Priya - quick answers and technical notes below. Thanks for the quick turnaround on data.

Shadow deployment: yes - we'll provision a shadow endpoint you can call in parallel (no writeback) so outputs can be compared against current routing decisions. That's our standard approach for features like routing suggestions.

Latency definition: we measure p95 from API receive (Redwood ingress) -> last token emitted; network round-trip will add variable client-side latency. For most customers p95 <200ms is achievable with batching and the model profiles we discussed - we'll instrument and report observed p95 in week 1 baseline.

Access checklist (technical details):
- Preferred: cross-account IAM role with the following policy (we'll provide least-privilege template). Role ARN is ideal because it avoids presigned URL expiry.
- If using presigned URLs, please provide a 7-day expiry and notify us when the bucket has been updated.
- Data format: NDJSON/JSONL preferred; include fields: ticket_id, created_at, text_body, metadata_tags. Attachments can be referenced by S3 path.
- Sample size: 1k-2k tickets for initial eval; we'll request additional samples if we see coverage gaps.

Prompt/eval notes:
- We'll run the provided prompt_set_v1.jsonl against a baseline smaller model first to surface obvious failure modes.
- Please include an internal owner for label adjudication - we'll need a small set (10-15) of adjudicated examples for rubric calibration.

I'll create a staging repo and share a Drive link with the eval dashboard by EOD Monday.

Neha Kapoor
